Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:21:00 -0000
Subject: Unexpected duplicate metered lines in Sept invoice

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing duplicated metered line items on our AWS Marketplace invoice for the billing period Aug 30 - Sep 13. Two separate SKUs appear to have recorded the same usage block for several large runs from our ingestion cluster; the attached CSV shows the line-level evidence (columns: timestamp, sku, resource_id, tokens). Our finance team is seeing a ~14% overcharge relative to expected consumption.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is something on the seller (Redwood) side — i.e., two listings accidentally both reporting the same usage — or if this is an AWS-side metering duplication? Nimbus needs the reconciliation and any proposed credit before their month-end close (9/20).

Attached: nimbus-metering-delta.csv

Thanks,
Sophie Tran

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected duplicate metered lines in Sept invoice

Thanks for the ping — I pulled the seller-side metering events for the period and started a quick diff against the Nimbus CSV. Preliminary findings:

- Redwood raw meter events (post-ingest) show a single consumption event per run keyed by resource_id and timestamp. No duplicate events on our ingestion side.
- The bookkeeping/aggregation layer maps internal usage to marketplace SKUs via a mapping table. I found an edge case in the SKU mapping: when a job runs across a capacity boundary we emit two aggregated report rows (one for reserved-pool SKU, one fallback on-demand SKU) and we include a 1-second overlap timestamp in both aggregates. That overlap can surface as two line items in the marketplace CSV if AWS re-aggregates differently.

Attached a small snippet of the mapping logic and the query I used: sku-mapping-snippet.txt

Hypothesis: It's a SKU-mapping + aggregation boundary issue on Redwood that, when combined with AWS's re-aggregation/timestamp rounding, produces perceived duplicated lines. Low probability it's a pure AWS duplication — but AWS still needs to confirm their case.

Next steps I propose:
1) We confirm overlap buckets and update aggregation to dedupe 1-second overlaps (short-term fix).
2) Marissa can draft a credit proposal while we validate numbers; mark as provisional.
3) Open a support case with AWS (if they confirm duplicate ingestion on their side we need their credit flow; if it's our mapping we will issue the credit ourselves).

I'll run the overlap dedupe in a dry-run and post numbers by EOD.

-Karthik
Senior Engineer, Inference Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

I've prepared a provisional credit proposal PDF (credit-proposal-DB-7782.pdf) that outlines:

- Accounting impact: reduce Sept revenue recognized to match credit period; treat as contra-revenue for Q3 close.
- Tax/VAT handling: tag credit as negative invoice at the marketplace level and loop in Finalt Tax for VAT documentation.

Action items:

- Jasmine: help get Nimbus to confirm they accept a provisional credit while we complete the root-cause patch. If AWS confirms their duplication we will coordinate a marketplace-level credit; otherwise Redwood will fund the credit and then we will consider a follow-up with AWS.

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Marketplace Metered Line Items — Nimbus Analytics (usage delta)

Hi all,

Thanks for the details and the attachments — we replicated the issue in our test aggregation pipeline. Root cause: a timestamp rounding bug in AWS re-aggregation that, for certain cross-boundary reports, duplicated a 1-second overlapped bucket. This produces two separate invoice lines in the marketplace invoice export. We've created AWS case 123456789 and attached our case summary (aws-case-123456789.pdf).

Resolution steps AWS will perform:
- Issue a marketplace-level credit equal to the duplicated units for the affected lines (we estimate the customer-facing credit will match your provisional numbers once you send the reconciled CSV).
- Backfill corrected invoice CSVs for Nimbus upon request.
- Provide a permanent fix to the re-aggregation routine (ETA: 4 weeks).

Next steps for this thread:
1) Karthik/Redwood: send final reconciled line-level CSV referencing marketplace invoice line ids so we can reconcile amounts on our side.
2) Marissa: AWS will accept a HubSpot/Drive link for the credit memo request; include the provisional credit proposal and confirm tax handling.
3) Nimbus: confirm acceptance of an AWS marketplace credit or Redwood-funded credit (if you prefer Redwood to expedite we can issue a Redwood credit while AWS completes their case).

I'll keep AWS case 123456789 open and update it after you provide the CSV.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Billing
marketplace-billing@amazon.com

Attachments: aws-case-123456789.pdf
